title: The Lost Colony of Roanoke — 115 people gone, one word left behind
sources: Wikipedia: Roanoke Colony — Sir Walter Raleigh's attempts to found the first permanent English settlement in North America; in 1587 about 115 colonists, including Governor John White's pregnant daughter Eleanor and her husband Ananias Dare, settled on Roanoke Island (present-day North Carolina); on 18 August 1587 Virginia Dare was born; the colonists persuaded White to return to England for help; the Spanish Armada crisis kept every able ship in England, and White could not return until 1590; he landed on 18 August 1590, his granddaughter's third birthday, finding 'CRO' carved on a tree and 'CROATOAN' on a palisade post; the houses had been dismantled, his own trunks dug up and looted, and the boats were gone; the colonists had agreed to carve their destination, with a cross pattée as a sign of distress — there was none; White believed they had gone to Croatoan Island, but the Hopewell's anchor cable snapped and the search was abandoned; he never found them; theories include assimilation with the Croatan (ancestors of the Hatteras), and Mark Horton's excavation found European artifacts, including part of a sword and part of a gun, at a Native village site on Hatteras Island; tree rings show 1587 was the worst growing season in 800 years.

Images (public domain / CC0, Wikimedia Commons): John White's watercolours and maps (1585) and Theodor de Bry's engravings (1590–91); Nicholas Hilliard's miniature of Sir Walter Raleigh (c. 1585); 'The baptism of Virginia Dare' (1876); illustrations of the CROATOAN discovery (1890, 1906); the Fort Raleigh reconstruction and the 2009 excavation
Film (public domain): Louis Lumière, 'Barque sortant du port' (1897); USCGC Eagle under sail (US Coast Guard, 2026); NOAA, shipwrecks off the North Carolina coast — illustrative
Music: Mussorgsky, The Old Castle (Pictures at an Exhibition), public domain

post.facebook:
In 1590, a governor came back to his colony in America. All 115 people were gone. The only clue was one word, carved into a post: CROATOAN.

The Roanoke Colony was England's first real try at settling America, sent by Sir Walter Raleigh. In 1587 about 115 men, women and children landed on Roanoke Island in today's North Carolina, and weeks later Governor John White's granddaughter Virginia Dare was born — the first English child born in the New World. The colonists sent White back to England for supplies. Then the Spanish Armada came, and every English ship was kept at home.

It took White three years to return. He landed on his granddaughter's third birthday. The houses were taken apart, his chests dug up and looted, the boats gone — and every single person with them. They had agreed to carve their destination, and a cross if in danger. There was no cross: just CRO on a tree and CROATOAN on a post. Then a storm snapped the ship's anchor cable and White had to sail away. He never saw his family again.

Today archaeologists on Hatteras Island — the old Croatoan — have found English sword and gun parts in a Native village. Did they simply join the tribe? 👇

youtube.description:
In 1590, a governor came back to his colony in America. All 115 people were gone. The only clue was one word, carved into a post: CROATOAN.

The Lost Colony of Roanoke: in 1587 Sir Walter Raleigh's colonists settled Roanoke Island, where Virginia Dare became the first English child born in the New World. Governor John White sailed home for supplies, but the Spanish Armada kept him in England until 1590. He returned to find the settlement dismantled, his belongings looted and the word CROATOAN carved on a post — but no cross, the agreed sign of danger. A snapped anchor cable ended his search. Excavations on Hatteras Island (the old Croatoan) have since found English sword and gun parts in a Native village.
